samples.summary: Workflow content is shipped as a committed `git apply`-ready patch, routing the `workflows` permission boundary the trust model rests on through reviewer diligence instead
samples.evidence: The file opens `APPLY WITH: git apply docs/tasks/active/…patch` and explains that it exists because "The agent App … cannot push `.github/workflows/**`". That inability is not an oversight: agent-review-panel.yml:46-52 says the `workflow_run` trigger is chosen "because" of it ("with `checks:write`, the permission the 'check runs are author-unforgeable' property rests on"), and the co-committed lessons file repeats it ("A permission the agent lacks may be the security model, not a gap"). The same repo already records this exact anti-pattern as a prior blocking panel finding (scripts/agent/rounds.test.mjs:188-193, on a previous `.patch` under `docs/tasks/active/`), and the lessons file added by this very commit says "A blocked half does not ship as a `.patch` file". samples.summary: The author/fixer paths mint an UNSCOPED GitHub App installation token from a mutable action tag, which is what makes the gate-2 forgery above reachable
samples.evidence: agent-implement.yml:117-122 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-109 call `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` with `app-id`/`private-key` and NO `permission-*` inputs, so the minted token carries every permission the installation holds — handed to a job that then executes model-directed code with the branch checked out. Every other consumer in this repo scopes the token explicitly and pins the action to an immutable SHA for exactly this reason: agent-review-panel.yml:1483-1493 ("Pinned to an immutable commit SHA (not the movable @v1 tag) for supply-chain safety — this action handles the App private key", plus `permission-pull-requests: write` / `permission-issues: write`), agent-rerun.yml:94-98, agent-loop.yml:83-87, ci-report.yml:86-94. Pre-existing and outside the diff, but the diff's whole premise is that these gates are unforgeable, and the token scope is what decides that.

The token is not merely held in the job: agent-implement.yml:197-200 checks out the branch with it and agent-implement.yml:354-357 hands it straight to anthropics/claude-code-action as github_token, i.e. to model-directed execution; agent-iterate-ci.yml:111-115 does the checkout equivalent, and that file's own comment (lines 117-126) calls the branch code attacker-influenceable. Every other consumer scopes and SHA-pins for exactly this reason (agent-fix.yml:119-130, agent-review-panel.yml:1485-1493, agent-rerun.yml:94-98, agent-loop.yml:83-87, ci-report.yml:86-94, agent-summarize.yml:116-120, agent-review-on-demand.yml:112-116), with agent-fix.yml:125-127 stating the least-privilege rationale verbatim - the convention is broken precisely in the two jobs that run untrusted/model-directed code. The gate-2 linkage also holds: scripts/agent/checks.mjs:159-164 accepts any check run matching name + conclusion with no app.slug/app-id provenance check, so an over-privileged token with Checks:write lets the author agent mint its own agent-review-* check runs. The installation is known to be broadly privileged (agent-implement.yml:126 requires Administration:read; other workflows use contents/issues/pull-requests write). Secondary vector confirmed: the mutable @v1 tag handles secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, so a retagged action reads the App private key. No guard elsewhere narrows the token or validates check-run provenance; in-lane (access control / excessive privilege / secret handling) and blocking.

finding.summary: Gate 1b's `CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES` is far narrower than the CI-defining surface it claims to cover — a branch can gut CI via `package.json` / `scripts/verify-*.mjs` / `harness.config.json` and still auto-promote, while the new hand-off comment tells the human reviewer the run executed main's CI definition.
finding.evidence: Gate 1b refuses promotion only when a changed path starts with `.github/workflows/` or `.github/actions/` (mark-ready.mjs:175, 189). But `ci.yml` contains almost no test logic: `verify-self` runs `pnpm verify:self` (.github/workflows/ci.yml:308) and `verify-integration` runs `pnpm verify:integration` (ci.yml:752), both resolved from the MERGE REF's `package.json` ("verify:self": "node ./scripts/verify-self.mjs", package.json:25) and executed from the branch's `scripts/verify-self.mjs`. The `changes` job likewise runs the branch's `node ./scripts/changed-areas.mjs` (ci.yml:149) and its `heavy` output gates every step of `verify-browser` / `verify-integration` / coverage (ci.yml:317-321, 484-487, 593-596). ATTACK: under gate 1b's own stated threat model ("an `agent:managed` human PR is on this promote path and is not restricted", mark-ready.mjs:28), the author pushes a commit that changes only `scripts/verify-self.mjs` (or the `verify:self` script in `package.json`, or `harness.config.json` so `heavy=false`) so the lanes no-op. `.github/workflows/**` is untouched, so `branchEditsCiDefinition` returns false, gate 1b passes, gate 1 sees a genuinely green run of the genuine `ci.yml`, and the PR is auto-promoted. The repo already knows the real surface: `harness.config.json`'s `ciConfig` list (harness.config.json:52-62) names `harness.config.json`, `scripts/changed-areas.mjs`, `scripts/verify-*.mjs`, `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `knip.json` alongside `.github/workflows/**` — gate 1b uses none of them, and `ciConfig` only forces a full run rather than refusing promotion. The harm is amplified rather than mitigated by this delta: the hand-off comment now asserts "the branch changes no workflow definition, so that run executed the CI file on `main` rather than one the branch supplied" (mark-ready.mjs:320-322) and the design doc's honest "WHAT THIS DOES NOT GUARANTEE" paragraph was replaced with "Gate 1b closes that" (mark-ready.mjs:19) — a gate that reads as covered to

verdict.reason: Verified in-tree. Gate 1b's CI_DEFINING_PREFIXES is literally only [".github/workflows/", ".github/actions/"] (mark-ready.mjs:175) and is the sole test in branchEditsCiDefinition (mark-ready.mjs:189), feeding ciDefinitionGate (mark-ready.mjs:210, gate list :236-241). But ci.yml's test logic is not in the workflow: verify-self does a bare actions/checkout@v4 (ci.yml:289) — the PR merge ref on pull_request — then `pnpm verify:self` (ci.yml:308) resolving through the merge ref's package.json:25 to the branch's scripts/verify-self.mjs; same for verify:integration (ci.yml:752, package.json:27) and the branch's scripts/changed-areas.mjs (ci.yml:149) whose `heavy` output gates coverage and both heavy jobs (ci.yml:317-329, 486, 595). So a branch touching only scripts/verify-*.mjs, the verify:* script in package.json, or harness.config.json gutts CI while branchEditsCiDefinition returns false and gate 1 still sees a green run of the genuine ci.yml. The repo already names that surface in harness.config.json:52-62 (ciConfig includes harness.config.json, scripts/changed-areas.mjs, scripts/verify-*.mjs, package.json, knip.json), and ciConfig only forces a full run/label (changed-areas.mjs:403-413) — it never refuses promotion. No compensating guard exists on the promote path: agent-review-panel.yml:1463-1465 gates only on ci conclusion + no blocking findings, and 1475/1508 run main's copy of the gate script but re-validate nothing about which test scripts ran; mark-ready.mjs:28 concedes an agent:managed human PR is unrestricted here. The delta amplifies the risk by asserting to the human reviewer that "the branch changes no workflow definition, so that run executed the CI file on `main`" (mark-ready.mjs:320-322) and replacing the caveat with "Gate 1b closes that" (mark-ready.mjs:19). Real, reachable, in-lane (a promotion/authorization gate that reads as covered but is bypassable via a branch-controlled input); no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Gate 1b's evidence (`pulls/{n}/files`) is diffed against the PR's BASE ref, which the PR author can change at will and which is not pinned to the SHA gate 1 read — retargeting the base after CI starts empties the file list and lets a workflow-editing branch through.
finding.evidence: `branchEditsCiDefinition` asks `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/files` (mark-ready.mjs:183), which returns the base..head diff for the PR's CURRENT base branch — a mutable, author-controlled field — whereas gate 1's evidence is a CI run pinned to `pr.headRefOid` (mark-ready.mjs:158, 166). ATTACK (same threat model as the gate: a collaborator opening an `agent:managed` PR): (1) push branch `x` containing a gutted `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; (2) open the PR from that head against `main`, so CI's `pull_request: branches: ["main"]` trigger (ci.yml:9-10) fires and runs the branch's gutted `ci.yml` on the merge ref, concluding green; the panel starts on `workflow_run: requested` and `promote` waits for the conclusion (agent-review-panel.yml:1454-1462); (3) before the promote job runs `mark-ready`, retarget the PR's base to another branch in the same repo that already carries the same gutted `ci.yml`. Retargeting neither cancels the already-created CI run nor changes `headRefOid`, so gate 1 still reads `success` — but `pulls/{n}/files` now diffs against the new base and reports no `.github/workflows/**` entry, so gate 1b passes and the PR is promoted with the hand-off comment claiming main's CI definition ran. A slower variant needs no race: retarget after the refusal, then `@claude rerun`, whose `workflow_run: completed` with `run_attempt > 1` is explicitly admitted by the panel gate (agent-review-panel.yml:164-169). I could not execute this to confirm GitHub does not cancel the in-flight run on retarget, hence medium confidence. A base-independent check (e.g. comparing the head tree's `.github/workflows/**` against the default branch, or reading the run's own `head_sha` tree) would not have this property.

verdict.reason: Verified as described. Gate 1b's evidence is `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/files` (mark-ready.mjs:183), a base-relative diff whose base ref is author-mutable, while gate 1 is SHA-pinned to `pr.headRefOid` (mark-ready.mjs:166, query at :158). The script never reads `baseRefName`/`baseRefOid` — the PR view fetches only `number,body,isDraft,labels,headRefName,headRefOid,url` (mark-ready.mjs:122-128) — so nothing ties the file-list evidence to the ref the green CI run was produced against. No guard elsewhere closes it: the promote job's condition is only ci conclusion + panel-not-blocked + non-empty PR (agent-review-panel.yml:1463-1465), and the panel gate filters only on run path, head repo, and action/run_attempt (agent-review-panel.yml:164-169), explicitly admitting `run_attempt > 1` (the no-race rerun variant). `ciConclusion` is newest-run-wins by id (checks.mjs:116-126), so an already-created green run for the head SHA survives a retarget; `ci.yml:9-10`'s `branches: ["main"]` filter governs run creation, not survival. Head must be in-repo (agent-review-panel.yml:167), so the actor already has push access to create the alternate base branch carrying the same gutted ci.yml. Result: a documented security gate (mark-ready.mjs:16-29) is bypassable and the hand-off comment then asserts the opposite (mark-ready.mjs:320-322) — a weakened permission/evidence gate in this lens's lane, blocking at major.
